# omada_ips_whitelist (Resource)

Exempts a traffic source from IPS/IDS inspection (the IPS allow list).

~> **This weakens a security control for whatever it covers.** An exempted source is no longer inspected, so use it for a specific false positive rather than to quiet the log.

An entry is nothing but its three fields, so changing any of them is a different rule and replaces the entry — the controller offers no update verb for it either.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Exempt a network from IPS/IDS inspection.
#
# This switches off a security control for whatever it covers, so reach for it
# to clear a specific false positive — not to quiet a noisy log.
resource "omada_ips_whitelist" "guest" {
  direction      = 1
  traffic_type   = 1 # 1 pairs with a network id
  traffic_source = omada_network.guest.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `direction` (Number) Controller enum for the traffic direction the exemption applies to. TP-Link does not document the values; the UI writes `1`. Check the controller before choosing another.
- `traffic_source` (String) ID of the exempted object — a network id when `traffic_type` is `1` (see the `omada_networks` data source).
- `traffic_type` (Number) Controller enum selecting what `traffic_source` identifies. `1` pairs with a network id.

### Optional

- `site` (String) Site name. Defaults to the primary site. Changing forces replacement.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `site_id` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By entry ID, or "<site>/<id>".
terraform import omada_ips_whitelist.guest 6a64dcbdbb62a10bd62c4ddd
```
